examples.solution_text:
Each square uses $4$ matches.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage number}&1&2&3\\\hline\text{Number of matches}&4&8&12\end{array}$
$\begin{aligned}4&=4\times1\\8&=4\times2\\12&=4\times3\end{aligned}$
The number of matches is $4$ times the stage number. Adding $4$ continues the pattern; multiplying the stage number by $4$ finds any stage directly.
At stage $8$:
$4\times8=32$ matches.

examples.question_text:
Separate shapes use the same number of matches each, with no shared matches.
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Number of shapes}&2&4&6\\\hline\text{Number of matches}&16&32&48\end{array}$
Describe the relationship between the number of shapes and the number of matches using multiplication.
examples.solution_text:
Two shapes use $16$ matches. Since $8\times2=16$, each shape uses $8$ matches.
Check the other entries:
$\begin{aligned}8\times4&=32\\8\times6&=48\end{aligned}$
The number of matches is $8$ times the number of shapes.

examples.question_text:
A pattern table shows these counts:
$\begin{array}{c|ccc}\text{Stage number}&3&5&8\\\hline\text{Number of matches}&18&30&48\end{array}$
Describe one multiplication relationship and show that it fits every entry.
examples.solution_text:
Since $6\times3=18$, try multiplying the stage number by $6$.
$\begin{aligned}6\times3&=18\\6\times5&=30\\6\times8&=48\end{aligned}$
Every entry fits. The number of matches is $6$ times the stage number.

examples.derivation: The diagram defines separate groups of one, two and three squares, with no shared sides: 4, 8 and 12 matches. These equal 4×1, 4×2 and 4×3, so the number of matches is four times the stage number. Stage 8 uses 4×8=32 matches. This adapts the separate-shape multiplication pattern in Foundation Q2, lines 2305–2329 and image121.png, without introducing equations or graphing.

16 ÷ 2 = 8, 32 ÷ 4 = 8 and 48 ÷ 6 = 8. Thus each separate shape uses eight matches, and the number of matches is eight times the number of shapes. Multiplication checks reproduce all three entries. The supplied table is sufficient without a shape diagram.
18 ÷ 3 = 6 identifies the multiplier. Independently checking 6 × 3 = 18, 6 × 5 = 30 and 6 × 8 = 48 confirms every entry. The number of matches is six times the stage number.
